name: Turks and Caicos
title: Holidays in Turks and Caicos
intro: A British Overseas Territory of low coral islands, with powder-white Grace Bay and some of the clearest water in the Caribbean. Here's what Turks and Caicos is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: Turquoise water lapping a white sand beach in Turks and Caicos
facts_note: Hurricane season runs from June to November, peaking from August to October. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: December to May is the best time, sunny and dry with a cooling trade wind, though it's also the priciest. June and July are hot but usually fine. Hurricane season peaks from August to October, when some hotels close.

things.name: Grace Bay Beach
things.blurb: Twelve miles of soft white sand and calm, clear water on Providenciales.

things.name: Smith's Reef and Bight Reef
things.blurb: Snorkel straight off the beach over coral, turtles and rays.

things.name: Chalk Sound
things.blurb: A startlingly turquoise lagoon dotted with little rocky islands.

things.name: Iguana Island
things.blurb: Boat trips to Little Water Cay, home to rare rock iguanas.

things.name: Grand Turk
things.blurb: The small capital island, with a lighthouse, donkeys and wall diving.

things.name: Whale watching
things.blurb: Humpback whales pass between January and April.

faqs.question: Is Turks and Caicos expensive?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's one of the priciest Caribbean destinations, as nearly everything is imported.

faqs.question: How do you get to Turks and Caicos from the UK?
faqs.answer: British Airways flies via Antigua, or connect through Miami or another US airport.

faqs.question: What is the best beach in Turks and Caicos?
faqs.answer: Grace Bay is the famous one. Taylor Bay and Sapodilla Bay are shallow, calm and quieter.

faqs.question: Do you need a visa for Turks and Caicos?
faqs.answer: No. UK passport holders can visit for up to 90 days. Connecting through the US needs an ESTA.
